title: Human Metapneumovirus Diagnosis, Pathogenesis, and Therapeutics
abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a globally prevalent respiratory pathogen that causes acute respiratory infections across all age groups, with the greatest disease burden in young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Clinical manifestations range from mild upper respiratory tract symptoms, including cough, wheezing, and sore throat, to severe lower respiratory tract disease such as bronchiolitis, pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and secondary bacterial infections that may require intensive care and mechanical ventilation. Despite its widespread circulation and substantial healthcare impact, important aspects of hMPV transmission, pathogenesis, and host immune responses remain incompletely understood, hindering the development of effective therapeutics and vaccines. This review summarizes the current knowledge of hMPV epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnostics, pathogenesis, and prevention strategies, with emphasis on recent outbreaks that highlight its seasonal and geographic variability. We discuss the viral life cycle and the contributions of the major surface glycoproteins—fusion (F), attachment (G), and small hydrophobic (SH) proteins—to viral infectivity, immune evasion, and disease progression. Advances in molecular diagnostics, including reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), next-generation sequencing, metagenomic approaches, and nanopore sequencing, are also examined. While supportive care remains the cornerstone of clinical management, existing antiviral therapies demonstrate limited and inconsistent efficacy. Emerging preventive and therapeutic strategies, including mRNA-based vaccines and neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, offer promising avenues for disease control. Improved understanding of hMPV biology and host-pathogen interactions will be critical for developing effective interventions to reduce the global burden of this increasingly recognized respiratory pathogen.

title_zh: 人偏肺病毒 诊断,发病机制,and Therapeutics
source_body_en: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a globally prevalent respiratory pathogen that causes acute respiratory infections across all age groups, with the greatest disease burden in young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Clinical manifestations range from mild upper respiratory tract symptoms, including cough, wheezing, and sore throat, to severe lower respiratory tract disease such as bronchiolitis, pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and secondary bacterial infections that may require intensive care and mechanical ventilation. Despite its widespread circulation and substantial healthcare impact, important aspects of hMPV transmission, pathogenesis, and host immune responses remain incompletely understood, hindering the development of effective therapeutics and vaccines. This review summarizes the current knowledge of hMPV epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnostics, pathogenesis, and prevention strategies, with emphasis on recent outbreaks that highlight its seasonal and geographic variability. We discuss the viral life cycle and the contributions of the major surface glycoproteins—fusion (F), attachment (G), and small hydrophobic (SH) proteins—to viral infectivity, immune evasion, and disease progression. Advances in molecular diagnostics, including reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), next-generation sequencing, metagenomic approaches, and nanopore sequencing, are also examined. While supportive care remains the cornerstone of clinical management, existing antiviral therapies demonstrate limited and inconsistent efficacy. Emerging preventive and therapeutic strategies, including mRNA-based vaccines and neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, offer promising avenues for disease control. Improved understanding of hMPV biology and host-pathogen interactions will be critical for developing effective interventions to reduce the global burden of this increasingly recognized respiratory pathogen.

title: Emerging Trends in the Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Management of Human Metapneumovirus-Associated Respiratory Infections
abstract: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.

source_records.abstract: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.

abstract_zh: 引言:人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是一种重要的呼吸道病原体,可在不同年龄段人群中引发感染,尤其是在幼儿、免疫功能低下者及老年人中。尽管其具有重要的临床意义,但目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物或针对人偏肺病毒的特异性治疗方法,亟需进一步研究治疗和预防策略。方法:通过系统性文献综述,检索同行评议期刊、临床试验及近期研究,重点关注人偏肺病毒感染。提取并分析数据,以评估抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体、免疫调节剂及疫苗候选物的有效性。结果:研究表明,人偏肺病毒主要靶向呼吸道上皮细胞,触发免疫应答,这些免疫应答既有助于病毒清除,也会导致疾病发病机制。正在研发的治疗方法,包括融合抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂,显示出潜力,但仍需进一步验证。免疫调节剂和中草药可能提供支持性益处,但其对人偏肺病毒的有效性尚未得到证实。疫苗研发取得进展,多个候选疫苗已进入临床前及早期临床阶段。讨论:由于人偏肺病毒的季节性流行、与其他呼吸道病毒的临床相似性以及缺乏特异性治疗方法,该病毒继续对公共卫生构成重大负担。该病毒通过多种机制逃避免疫应答,导致疾病严重程度增加,尤其是在易感人群中。尽管目前主要采用支持性治疗,但新兴的抗病毒药物和疫苗可能为未来提供解决方案。改善诊断可及性、提高公众意识及开展针对性研究对于控制人偏肺病毒感染至关重要。结论:由于缺乏针对性治疗方法和疫苗,人偏肺病毒继续对公共卫生构成挑战。针对抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体及疫苗的持续研究对于有效疾病管理至关重要。亟需进一步临床试验以确立安全有效的治疗方案。

title: Viral etiology and predictors of hospitalization in adults younger than 65 years with laboratory-confirmed respiratory viral infections in the pre-COVID era
abstract: Respiratory viral tract infections (VRTIs) are generally considered more severe in older adults, while their clinical impact in younger adults remains less well characterized. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of adults aged 18–64 years with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus (hMPV), or parainfluenza virus (PIV) infection during the 2016–2018 respiratory seasons. Among 172 patients, 110 had influenza, 31 RSV, 17 hMPV, and 14 PIV infections. Hospitalization occurred in 64.0% of patients overall, with rates of 53.6% for influenza, 77.4% for RSV, and 87.1% for hMPV/PIV infections. Chronic respiratory disease, neutrophilia, and hMPV/PIV infection were independently associated with hospitalization. Chronic respiratory disease and previous respiratory tract infection were independently associated with lower odds of short-term favorable outcome, whereas detectable eosinophils were associated with improved recovery. Ninety-day mortality was low across viral groups. Age was not independently associated with hospitalization or short-term recovery within this restricted age range. These findings highlight substantial morbidity associated with VRTIs in adults younger than 65 years and underscore the need for greater attention to this population, which remains less well characterized than older adults.

title: In silico conservation and HLA-binding profiles of HMPV F and G protein epitopes: implications for universal vaccine development.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a significant cause of respiratory infection, yet no licensed vaccine exists. Variability across viral subgroups, particularly in the attachment (G) protein, can complicate universal design. We assessed the immunogenetic regions in the fusion (F) and G proteins to identify stable vaccine targets. METHODS: We analyzed N = 324 Pittsburgh and N = 655 global HMPV genomes (2017-2022) for genome diversity per viral subgroup. Previously identified epitope sequences were obtained from the Immune Epitope DataBase (IEDB) for F and G proteins and sequence similarity was determined. Using NetMHCpan-4.1, we identified and computed inferred human leukocyte antigen (HLA) binding affinities for 15 epitope variants (1 or 2 substitutions) against universally common human alleles. RESULTS: The F protein was highly conserved across all subgroups (>96% amino acid sequence identity). In the G protein, we identified a conserved epitope cluster (G3-G7) where epitope G7 was present in 91% of A2 genomes. Functional modeling of the G-protein epitope variants revealed that the majority of HLA alleles maintained or gained binding affinity, a subset exhibited diminished binding (escape), suggesting these regions are subject to ongoing antigenic drift. B-genotypes showed fewer retained binders and were notably underrepresented in the current epitope databases. CONCLUSION: The conserved F protein remains an optimal target for neutralization, while the G3-G7 cluster provides a robust secondary target for T-cell mediated immunity. A bivalent vaccine strategy could pair the stable F protein with these high-frequency G-protein epitopes to elicit an immune response. This approach addresses the A2 subgroup, and incorporating B-genotypes through ongoing surveillance and epitope mapping will be essential to achieve comprehensive, multi-antigen coverage across circulating HMPV strains.

title_zh: 人偏肺病毒(HMPV)F和G蛋白表位的体外保守性和HLA结合特征:对开发通用疫苗的启示。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a significant cause of respiratory infection, yet no licensed vaccine exists. Variability across viral subgroups, particularly in the attachment (G) protein, can complicate universal design. We assessed the immunogenetic regions in the fusion (F) and G proteins to identify stable vaccine targets. METHODS: We analyzed N = 324 Pittsburgh and N = 655 global HMPV genomes (2017-2022) for genome diversity per viral subgroup. Previously identified epitope sequences were obtained from the Immune Epitope DataBase (IEDB) for F and G proteins and sequence similarity was determined. Using NetMHCpan-4.1, we identified and computed inferred human leukocyte antigen (HLA) binding affinities for 15 epitope variants (1 or 2 substitutions) against universally common human alleles. RESULTS: The F protein was highly conserved across all subgroups (>96% amino acid sequence identity). In the G protein, we identified a conserved epitope cluster (G3-G7) where epitope G7 was present in 91% of A2 genomes. Functional modeling of the G-protein epitope variants revealed that the majority of HLA alleles maintained or gained binding affinity, a subset exhibited diminished binding (escape), suggesting these regions are subject to ongoing antigenic drift. B-genotypes showed fewer retained binders and were notably underrepresented in the current epitope databases. CONCLUSION: The conserved F protein remains an optimal target for neutralization, while the G3-G7 cluster provides a robust secondary target for T-cell mediated immunity. A bivalent vaccine strategy could pair the stable F protein with these high-frequency G-protein epitopes to elicit an immune response. This approach addresses the A2 subgroup, and incorporating B-genotypes through ongoing surveillance and epitope mapping will be essential to achieve comprehensive, multi-antigen coverage across circulating HMPV strains.
abstract_zh: 背景:人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是呼吸道感染的重要病原体,但目前尚无获批的疫苗。病毒亚群间的变异性,尤其是在附着(G)蛋白中,可能阻碍通用疫苗的设计。我们评估了F和G蛋白中的免疫遗传区域,以确定稳定的疫苗靶点。方法:我们分析了N = 324匹兹堡和N = 655全球HMPV 基因组(2017-2022),以评估各病毒亚群的基因组多样性。从免疫表位数据库(IEDB)获取了之前鉴定的F和G蛋白表位序列,并确定了序列相似性。利用NetMHCpan-4.1,我们鉴定了并计算了15个表位变体(1或2个取代)对普遍人类等位基因的推断人类白细胞抗原(HLA)结合亲和力。结果:F蛋白在所有亚群中高度保守(>96%的氨基酸序列同源性)。在G蛋白中,我们鉴定出一个保守的表位簇(G3-G7),其中表位G7在91%的A2亚群基因组中存在。G蛋白表位变体的功能建模显示,大多数HLA等位基因保持或增强了结合亲和力,而部分等位基因表现出结合亲和力下降(逃逸),这表明这些区域可能正在经历持续的抗原漂变。B型基因组显示出较少的保留结合位点,并且在当前的表位数据库中显著代表性不足。结论:高度保守的F蛋白仍然是中和的最优靶点,而G3-G7簇则为T细胞介导的免疫提供了稳健的次级靶点。一种双价疫苗策略可以将稳定的F蛋白与这些高频率的G蛋白表位结合,以引发有效的免疫应答。这种方法可以应对A2亚群,并通过持续的监测和表位映射纳入B型基因组,从而实现对流行HMPV株的全面、多抗原覆盖。

title: Immunogenicity and Safety of Coadministration of AS01E-Adjuvanted Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F Protein Vaccine and a COVID-19 mRNA Vaccine in Adult s Aged ≥50 Years: A Phase 3, Randomized, Noninferiority Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This trial evaluated coadministration of the AS01E-adjuvanted respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F protein-based vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) and an Omicron XBB.1.5-based coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) mRNA vaccine in ≥50-year-olds. METHODS: This phase 3, open-label, multicenter trial randomized ≥50-year-olds 1:1 to coadministration (Co-Ad group) or sequential administration approximately 1 month apart (Control group) of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccine. Primary objectives were to demonstrate noninferiority of humoral immune responses at 1 month postvaccination in terms of RSV-A, RSV-B, and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) neutralizing titers, with the upper limit of the 95% CI of adjusted geometric mean titer (GMT) group ratios (Control/Co-Ad) ≤1.50. Secondary objectives included assessment of reactogenicity up to 4 days and safety up to 6 months after vaccination. Noninferiority was achieved for RSV-A (GMT ratio: 1.12 [95% CI: .97-1.28]) and RSV-B (GMT ratio: 1.08 [95% CI: .94-1.23]) and marginally missed for SARS-CoV-2 Omicron XBB.1.5 (GMT ratio: 1.31 [95% CI: 1.13-1.51]). Within 4 days postvaccination, the most frequently reported solicited events were administration-site pain, myalgia, and fatigue. Most solicited events were of mild-to-moderate intensity, and the overall median duration was ≤3 days and comparable between groups. Unsolicited and serious adverse events were generally balanced between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 coadministered with a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine maintained an acceptable safety profile in ≥50-year-olds. The marginal miss of the noninferiority criterion for SARS-CoV-2 does not suggest clinically relevant interference. Therefore, the results support the coadministration of these vaccines. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials.gov.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

title: Enhanced respiratory syncytial virus surveillance of young children admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, 2019-2023.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

title: Under pressure: lessons learnt from rapid implementation of the respiratory syncytial virus maternal vaccine and infant nirsevimab in Sydney, Australia.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To share lessons learnt from the Sydney Local Health District (SLHD) rollout of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention products, and present data on immunisation uptake for mothers and babies in two maternity hospitals. TYPE OF SERVICE: Rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and the injectable, long-acting monoclonal antibody nirsevimab for newborn infants to protect them from RSV infection and hospitalisation. METHODS: Deidentified summary data from the electronic medical record on RSV immunisation status in two SLHD maternity hospitals were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used as a lens to reflect on the rollout process. RESULTS: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in two SLHD hospitals improved from 4% in the first month of rollout (February 2025) to a range of 70-74% from June to September 2025. As antenatal coverage improved, the number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with reason for refusal not recorded. Documentation of RSV immunisation status improved as the rollout progressed. LESSONS LEARNT: Engaging multidisciplinary leaders and clinicians is critical for a coordinated response and program rollout success. Leveraging existing education structures, staff meetings and using online prerecording can optimise clinician education. New programs take time to embed into routine clinical practice, and programs that involve delivering multiple immunisation products for distinct groups require clear messaging and systemic safeguards to prevent errors. Integrating immunisation into medical record workflows as standard practice can support program adoption and uptake.

title: Comprehensive Performance Verification of the Mindray MN2880 System in Detecting Respiratory Virus Nucleic Acids.
abstract: Objective To verify the clinical performance of the Mindray MN2880 system for simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A virus (IAV), influenza B virus (IBV), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) nucleic acids. Methods According to the CNAS-GL039:2019 and CNAS-GL037:2019 requirements for molecular diagnostic verification, we comprehensively evaluated the Mindray MN2880 multiplex respiratory virus assay across seven critical performance parameters: clinical concordance, limit of detection (LoD), repeatability, precision, cross-reactivity/interference resistance, daily QC, and contamination control. Results The Mindray MN2880 system demonstrated high diagnostic concordance with the reference method, with total percent agreements of 99.51% (95% CI: 99.00%-99.76%) for SARS-CoV-2, 99.93% (95% CI: 99.60%-99.99%) for IAV, and 100% for both IBV and RSV, and achieved clinically verified limits of detection (LoD: SARS-CoV-2 at 100 copies/mL, IAV/IBV/RSV at 200 copies/mL). Analytical precision was confirmed through 100% detection across negative/low/medium/high concentration panels with ≤ 3% CV for repeatability (Ct values) and ≤ 5% CV for inter-run precision. The assay exhibited 100% specificity against 6 clinically relevant pathogens, including Human Rhinovirus, parainfluenza virus, adenovirus, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Staphylococcus aureus, with no observed cross-reactivity. Moreover, the MN2880 system demonstrated robust interference resistance (100% detection of weakly-positive samples spiked with seven interferents), stable daily QC performance (100% valid controls across 115 consecutive runs), and 100% contamination prevention. Conclusion The MN2880 system satisfies key analytical benchmarks required for diagnostic use in respiratory virus multiplex testing, with performance verified against CNAS-GL039:2019 and CNAS-GL037:2019 standards.

title: Detection profiles and co-detection patterns of respiratory pathogens in hospitalized patients with acute respiratory infections after the COVID-19 pandemic in Nantong, China
abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory-pathogen circulation may have changed after relaxation of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) control measures. We characterized the pathogen spectrum, clinical-site distribution, age-specific patterns, co-detection patterns, and seasonality among hospitalized patients with acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) in Nantong, China. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 5,808 patients hospitalized with ARTIs at the Affiliated Hospital of Nantong University between December 2023 and December 2025. Respiratory specimens collected at admission were tested for 16 pathogens using multiplex real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Pathogen detection was compared by infection site, age group, and season. False discovery rate correction, multivariable logistic regression, and Cochran-Armitage trend tests were applied as appropriate. Results At least one pathogen was detected in 3,129 of 5,808 patients (53.87%). Single and mixed detections occurred in 2,103 (36.21%) and 1,026 (17.67%) patients, respectively. Klebsiella pneumoniae , Staphylococcus aureus , and Haemophilus influenzae were the most frequently detected bacterial targets. After false discovery rate correction, Mycoplasma pneumoniae , adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, H. influenzae , parainfluenza virus type III, and influenza B virus were more frequently detected in lower than upper respiratory tract infections (all q < 0.05). In adjusted analyses, M. influenzae remained associated with lower respiratory tract infections. pneumoniae detection peaked among children aged 6–17 years (30.92%, 81/262; P-trend < 0.001). Among patients with mixed detections, bacterial-bacterial pairs were most frequent, particularly S. Influenza A virus showed a marked winter peak (21.31% vs. 1.20–2.54% in other seasons; q < 0.001). Conclusion Hospitalized patients in eastern China showed frequent bacterial-target detection, age-related heterogeneity, and distinct seasonal patterns. The school-age peak in M. pneumoniae and the winter peak in influenza A virus support age- and season-informed surveillance. Because molecular detection cannot distinguish active infection from colonization, bacterial findings should be interpreted alongside clinical, culture, and biomarker data.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 在放松新冠病毒疾病2019(COVID-19)防控措施后,呼吸道病原体的流行可能发生了变化。我们分析了江苏省南通市住院急性呼吸道感染(ARTIs)患者中的病原体谱系、临床部位分布、年龄特异性模式、共检模式及季节性。方法 本回顾性横断面研究纳入了2023年12月至2025年12月期间在南通大学附属医院住院的5,808名急性呼吸道感染患者。在入院时收集的呼吸道标本通过多重实时定量聚合酶链反应检测了16种病原体。根据感染部位、年龄组和季节比较病原体检测结果。根据需要应用了错误发现率校正、多变量逻辑回归和Cochran-Armitage趋势检验。结果 在5,808名患者中,至少检测到一种病原体的有3,129名(53.87%)。单检和混合检分别发生在2,103名(36.21%)和1,026名(17.67%)患者中。克雷伯氏肺炎杆菌、金黄色葡萄球菌和流感嗜血杆菌是最常检测到的细菌靶标。在错误发现率校正后,肺炎支原体、腺病毒、人偏肺病毒、流感嗜血杆菌、副流感病毒III型和流感B病毒在下呼吸道感染中比上呼吸道感染更常见(所有q < 0.05)。在调整分析中,肺炎支原体仍与下呼吸道感染检测相关。肺炎支原体检测在6-17岁儿童中达到峰值(30.92%,81/262;P-trend < 0.001)。在混合检测患者中,细菌-细菌对最常见,特别是S. 腺病毒在冬季达到显著高峰(21.31% vs. 其他季节的1.20-2.54%;q < 0.001)。结论 江苏省南通市住院患者中表现出频繁的细菌靶标检测、年龄相关的异质性和独特的季节性模式。肺炎支原体的学龄儿童高峰和流感A病毒的冬季高峰支持基于年龄和季节的监测策略。由于分子检测无法区分活跃感染与定植,细菌检测结果应结合临床、培养和生物标志物数据进行解读。

title: Cynarin Targets Host CX3CR1 for Dual-Action Prophylaxis against RSV Infection and Pulmonary Pathology.
abstract: Safe, small-molecule prophylactic agents against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are critically lacking. Here, we identify Cynarin, an artichoke-derived dietary polyphenol, as a micromolar affinity CX3CR1 antagonist. Mechanistically, Cynarin confers dual-action protection through two distinct routes: it acts as a "chemical shield" to competitively block viral entry at the epithelial interface by binding CX3CR1, and through a separate CX3CR1-independent mechanism, exhibits intrinsic, virus-independent anti-inflammatory properties by directly suppressing macrophage activation. This target-based interaction was rigorously validated via biochemical and functional assays. In an RSV-infected mouse model, prophylactic administration of Cynarin demonstrated superior efficacy over therapeutic treatment. It significantly reduced pulmonary viral load, ameliorated lung consolidation, and potently suppressed the RSV-induced cytokine storm. Collectively, our findings establish a novel host-directed strategy utilizing Cynarin to target CX3CR1, highlighting the translational potential of food-derived bioactives in offering a dual prophylactic safeguard against viral infection and associated pulmonary pathology.
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Epidemiology and seasonality of respiratory syncytial virus among hospitalized pediatric patients with lower respiratory tract infections in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia (2017–2024)
abstract: Background Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) remains a significant public health concern globally, with distinct seasonal patterns in temperate regions, while tropical settings experience RSV year-round with seasonal fluctuations. This study investigated seasonality and exogenous factors influencing RSV cases among hospitalized children under 12 years in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia. Methods Weekly laboratory-confirmed RSV-positive cases among hospitalized pediatric patients presenting with acute lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) across 417 continuous WHO epidemiological weeks (EpiWeek 1, 2017 to EpiWeek 52, 2024) were analyzed using decomposition and autocorrelation functions. Relationships between RSV and co-circulating viruses, meteorological variables, and holidays were assessed via cross-correlation and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous variables (ARIMAX) modeling. Results A total of 6,545 (14.29%) samples were RSV-positive from a total of 45,817 tested. Historical peaks (July–September) were disrupted during 2020–2023 but re-established in 2024. The ARIMAX (2,0,4) (1,0,0) 52 model revealed that RSV dynamics were driven primarily by internal autoregressive patterns rather than meteorological factors. Major public holidays exhibited a significant dual effect, with an immediate decrease in reported cases ( p = 0.012) followed by a significant surge ( p = 0.014). Influenza activity was a significant predictor with a one-week lag ( p = 0.012). Conclusion The pandemic temporarily shifted RSV seasonality, which has since normalized. The associations with holiday periods and influenza activity suggests that behavioral factors and viral interference may influence RSV circulation. These findings emphasize the need for dynamic surveillance to optimize the timing of future RSV immunizations in Malaysia.

title: Data-driven forecasting of Flu, RSV, and COVID-19 related outcomes in the United States and Canada via Hankel dynamic mode decomposition.
abstract: The (large) season-to-season variability and limited dynamical history make the forecasting of infectious diseases a challenging problem. Here, we examine the extent to which advances in data-driven dynamical modeling can provide accurate predictions by benchmarking the performance of one such method, Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), on the 2024-2025 influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and COVID-19 seasons in the United States and Canada. Using Hankel-DMD, we generated weekly forecasts that were submitted to the Center for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) FluSight Forecast Hub and the University of Guelph's AI4CastingHub. Across both Hubs, we find that Hankel-DMD can provide high quality forecasts at the beginning and end of the season, but forecasts in the middle of the season suffer from significant overestimation of the season peak. This leads to worse than baseline performance on FluSight Forecast Hub, when submissions are evaluated across the entire season. Hankel-DMD is found to be the best among a small number of models that submitted enough forecasts against which to compare for forecasting influenza, RSV, and COVID-19 in Canada. As this was the first active year of AI4CastingHub, this suggests that Hankel-DMD may be especially useful when expertise is lacking for predicting infectious dynamics in new regions. To study how Hankel-DMD can be better equipped to provide accurate forecasts during the season peak, we explored whether DMD with memory, a recently developed approach for applying DMD to non-stationary dynamical systems, provides significant improvements. Retrospective analysis using DMD with memory shows promise in reducing overestimation during season peak, but the extent to which its optimal use can be achieved in a live forecasting setting remains to be seen. Collectively, our results demonstrate that Hankel-DMD has potential as an efficient and interpretable method for the forecasting of infectious diseases, while also highlighting a number of remaining methodological challenges which future work should aim to address.

title: A Confirmatory, Dual Center Nonhuman Primate Study on the Efficacy of Novel Oropharyngeal Spray Immunization With an Adenoviral Vector Vaccine Against RSV-Important Lessons Learned.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In a randomized, blinded, dual center study across two European primate research facilities, we evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA prime-oropharyngeal adenoviral boost vaccination strategy against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). METHODS: Rhesus macaques received an RSV fusion protein (F) DNA vaccine via electroporation, followed by two mucosal administrations of a recombinant adenovirus vector encoding the same antigen. Mock-vaccinated animals and a comparator group mimicking natural immunity induced by primary RSV infection were included as controls. Systemic and mucosal immune responses were monitored longitudinally. RESULTS: We detected robust cellular and humoral immune responses, but with some variability between the two centers. Nevertheless, RSV-vaccinated animals demonstrated markedly reduced viral replication in the upper and lower respiratory tract after RSV challenge infection. Unexpected RSV-specific immunity in the control group at one single study site prevented confirmation of the predefined primary endpoint. CONCLUSION: Our results support the potential of mucosal adenoviral boosting following DNA priming to induce protective immunity against RSV, while highlighting challenges associated with multi-center preclinical vaccine studies.

full_text: Abstract Introduction Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a significant viral pathogen associated with acute lower respiratory tract infections, particularly in elderly people. However, data on the clinical characteristics and outcomes of hMPV pneumonia among elderly people remain sparse. Methods We retrospectively reviewed data from 106 adult patients with polymerase chain reaction-confirmed hMPV infection and radiologically confirmed pneumonia diagnosed at Ewha Womans University Seoul Hospital between September 2022 and March 2025. Baseline characteristics, treatment, and clinical outcomes were analyzed by age group (< 80 vs. ≥80 years). Results The 106 patients had a median age of 71 years, and 37.8% of them were male. Hypertension (43.4%), malignancy (24.5%), and diabetes mellitus (24.5%) were the most common comorbidities. The patients were categorized into two age groups: <80 years (n = 79, 74.5%) and ≥ 80 years (n = 27, 25.5%). Patients aged ≥ 80 years had a significantly higher prevalence of hypertension (63.0% vs. 36.7%, p = 0.017), dementia (22.2% vs. 5.1%, p = 0.016), multilobar involvement (92.6% vs. 74.7%, p = 0.048), and pleural effusion (22.2% vs. 3.8%, p = 0.008). Additional microorganisms were detected in 32.1% of patients, with bacterial organisms alone (24.5%) being more common than viral organisms alone (5.7%); Haemophilus influenzae and Klebsiella pneumoniae were the most frequently detected bacteria. The overall hospitalization rate was 82.1% and was significantly higher among patients aged ≥ 80 years (96.3% vs. 77.2%, p = 0.038). ICU admission rates were numerically higher in patients aged ≥ 80 years (25.9% vs. 10.1%), although the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.150). In multivariable analysis among hospitalized patients, greater initial oxygen requirement was associated with longer hospitalization. Conclusion Adults aged ≥ 80 years with hMPV pneumonia had higher hospitalization rates and more severe clinical and radiologic features in age-group comparisons. These findings highlight the substantial clinical burden of hMPV pneumonia in older adults and the importance of careful assessment of disease severity at presentation. elements_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics and outcomes of human metapneumovirus (hMPV) pneumonia in elderly patients, as data on this specific population remain limited.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective study was conducted at Ewha Womans University Seoul Hospital, reviewing data from 106 adult patients with polymerase chain reaction-confirmed hMPV infection and radiologically confirmed pneumonia diagnosed between September 2022 and March 2025. Patients were divided into two age groups: <80 years (n = 79, 74.5%) and ≥80 years (n = 27, 25.5%).
elements_en.methods: The study involved reviewing medical records of patients with hMPV infection confirmed by polymerase chain reaction and pneumonia diagnosed radiologically. Baseline characteristics, treatment, and clinical outcomes were analyzed by age group.
elements_en.main_results: The median age of the patients was 71 years, with 37.8% being male. Hypertension, malignancy, and diabetes mellitus were the most common comorbidities. elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that older adults with hMPV pneumonia exhibit more severe clinical and radiologic features, which may contribute to higher hospitalization rates. This study provides novel insights into the clinical burden of hMPV pneumonia in the elderly population.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize the need for careful assessment of disease severity in older adults with hMPV pneumonia, which could inform targeted surveillance, diagnosis, and management strategies for this vulnerable group.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for selection bias. However, the evidence is strong due to the use of polymerase chain reaction and radiological confirmation of hMPV pneumonia, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

source_body_en: Methods We retrospectively reviewed data from 106 adult patients with polymerase chain reaction-confirmed hMPV infection and radiologically confirmed pneumonia diagnosed at Ewha Womans University Seoul Hospital between September 2022 and March 2025. Results The 106 patients had a median age of 71 years, and 37.8% of them were male. Conclusion Adults aged ≥ 80 years with hMPV pneumonia had higher hospitalization rates and more severe clinical and radiologic features in age-group comparisons. These findings highlight the substantial clinical burden of hMPV pneumonia in older adults and the importance of careful assessment of disease severity at presentation. Ethics declarations Ethics approval and consent to participate This study was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Ewha Womans University Seoul Hospital (IRB No. The requirement for informed consent was waived by the Institutional Review Board of Ewha Womans University Seoul Hospital due to the retrospective study design. All methods were performed in accordance with the relevant guidelines and regulations. title: Co-Assembly of Ribavirin and TMC353121 Nanoparticles for Enhanced Inhibition of Respiratory Syncytial Virus-Induced Pneumonia as an Alternative Therapy

source_records.title: Co-Assembly of Ribavirin and TMC353121 Nanoparticles for Enhanced Inhibition of Respiratory Syncytial Virus-Induced Pneumonia as an Alternative Therapy

priority_tier_reason: 高相关性，且具备高等级研究设计、全文证据或较强数据库/引用支持
full_text: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of acute respiratory infection requiring hospitalization in children worldwide. Although no combination therapies exist for RSV, ribavirin (RBA) and TMC353121 (TMC) can efficiently combat RSV through different mechanisms. We investigated the feasibility of formulating RBA and TMC into an RBA-TMC self-assembled nanoparticle (RTSN) and assessed its antiviral activity. Our results showed that RBA and TMC formed RTSN through hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking interactions. Cellular studies indicated that RTSN exhibited remarkable antioxidant, antiviral, and anti-inflammatory properties. RTSN showed antiviral efficacy, with a selectivity index of 43.8 and an effective concentration (EC50) of 10.9 μM. Moreover, RTSN was used to treat a mouse model of the respiratory syncytial virus-induced pneumonia (RSVIP) via multiple mechanisms, including mitigating oxidative stress, reducing viral load, and modulating macrophage polarization, while maintaining promising biosafety. Overall, this study presents an innovative treatment strategy for RSV and highlights the benefits of self-assembly technology in augmenting potential. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore an alternative therapy for RSV-induced pneumonia by investigating the feasibility of formulating ribavirin and TMC353121 into a self-assembled nanoparticle (RTSN) to enhance antiviral activity. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of acute respiratory infection requiring hospitalization in children worldwide.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved in vitro and in vivo experiments using a mouse model of respiratory syncytial virus-induced pneumonia (RSVIP). The research assessed the antiviral activity of RTSN through multiple mechanisms, including mitigating oxidative stress, reducing viral load, and modulating macrophage polarization.
analysis.methods: The researchers formulated ribavirin and TMC353121 into an RTSN using hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking interactions. Cellular studies were conducted to evaluate the antioxidant, antiviral, and anti-inflammatory properties of RTSN, and its efficacy was tested in a mouse model of RSV-induced pneumonia.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that RTSN exhibited antiviral efficacy with a selectivity index of 43.8 and an effective concentration (EC50) of 10.9 μM. Additionally, RTSN was found to have promising biosafety profiles.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating the potential of RTSN as an innovative treatment strategy for RSV. The study highlights the benefits of self-assembly technology in enhancing antiviral activity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that RTSN could offer a new therapeutic approach for RSV-induced pneumonia, potentially improving treatment options and reducing the burden of RSV-related hospitalizations in children.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro and in vivo experiments, which may not fully represent clinical outcomes. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on experimental models rather than human trials.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the feasibility of formulating ribavirin and TMC353121 into a self-assembled nanoparticle (RTSN) to enhance antiviral activity against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-induced pneumonia. The research demonstrates that RTSN can effectively combat RSV through multiple mechanisms, including reducing viral load and modulating macrophage polarization. The findings suggest that RTSN could serve as an innovative treatment strategy for RSV, highlighting the potential of self-assembly technology in antiviral applications. However, the study is limited to experimental models, and the evidence is moderate due to the absence of human clinical trials. The results may inform future research into alternative therapies for RSV and contribute to the development of more effective antiviral treatments.
